- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term (1–3d) forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in correction; delay forecast drop by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- Mean reversion is often overestimated; if price is above 3σ from 30d mean, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until reversion.
- For 30d forecasts, model tends to overestimate late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for days 25–30.
